observations.text: SP flew the airport traffic pattern to the desired standard for this Training Section, with the IP directing the pattern entry and nominating the position reports. Altitude at the initial point deviated by up to 350 feet and airspeed by up to 25 knots before the IP prompted the corrections. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent overflight of the LAP pattern points within 0.5 NM is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP entered and flew the airport traffic pattern without the IP directing or executing any part of the sequence, requiring only verbal indications for two of the standardized position reports. Altitude was contained within 300 feet and airspeed within 20 knots of the LAP pattern values, and the pattern points were overflown at the 0.5 NM limit. The deviations were recognized and corrected after the IP's verbal indications. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern according to the LAP and the instructions given by the ATC without any verbal prompting, maintaining proper spacing to the preceding traffic while clearing constantly. Altitude excursions reached 200 feet and airspeed 15 knots in the crosswind turn, and the pattern points were overflown within 0.3 NM. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern accurately and promptly, overflying every point described in the LAP within 0.2 NM and complying with all the ATC instructions. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading from each turn within 4 degrees. All the standardized position reports were given at the correct points and proper spacing to the other traffic was maintained while clearing constantly. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern with exceptional precision, overflying the LAP points within 0.1 NM with negligible deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading. The radio was monitored continuously and the position of each A/C was checked against its position report and the ATC instructions, so that spacing was managed in advance and no adjustment was required. The standardized position reports were given in full and on time throughout the pattern. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect visual reference technique on the downwind leg, did not overfly the points of the traffic pattern as they are described in the LAP, displacing the base turn point by 1.1 NM. Altitude decayed 400 feet and airspeed 30 knots below the LAP pattern values, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and executed the turn to final. The position reports were given only after the IP nominated them.

SP, due to a loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not check the position of the other A/C according to their position reports and the ATC instructions, and could not re-establish proper spacing without assistance. The initial point was overflown 1.3 NM wide of the LAP track with the altitude 350 feet low, with the result that the IP directed the extension of the downwind leg and executed the correcting turn. Constant clearing lapsed while the SP searched for the preceding traffic.

SP completed the airport traffic pattern within the desired standards, with the pattern points overflown at the 0.5 NM limit and with altitude and airspeed held at the 300 feet and 20 knots deviation limits. Two standardized position reports were given only after the IP's verbal indications, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-recognition of the pattern deviations is expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern according to the LAP and the ATC instructions without any verbal prompting from the IP, giving all the standardized position reports. Altitude deviations reached 180 feet and airspeed 14 knots in the turn to base, and the pattern points were overflown within 0.35 NM. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern accurately and promptly, overflying the LAP points within 0.2 NM and maintaining proper spacing to the traffic ahead while clearing constantly. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and the exit heading from each turn within 4 degrees. All the standardized position reports were given at the correct points and the radio was monitored continuously. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern with exceptional precision, holding the LAP pattern altitude, airspeed and exit headings with negligible deviations and overflying every point within 0.1 NM. The position of the other A/C was checked against each position report and the ATC instructions, so that proper spacing was maintained without any correction being required. Standardized phraseology was used on every transmission and clearing was continuous. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and pitch technique on the downwind leg, did not maintain the LAP pattern altitude and airspeed, allowing the aircraft to descend 420 feet low and to decelerate 28 knots below the pattern speed. The base turn was started 1.2 NM beyond the point described in the LAP, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and executed part of the turn to final. The SP did not recognize the deviations before the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the downwind leg, did not monitor the radio for the position reports of the other A/C and lost the required spacing to the preceding traffic. Altitude at the initial point was 380 feet high and the point was overflown 1.4 NM wide of the LAP track, with the result that the IP directed an orbit and made the position report on the SP's behalf. Clearing was not maintained during the corrective maneuver.

SP, due to a late start of the descent from the initial point, did not overfly the points of the traffic pattern as they are described in the LAP, reaching the base turn point at the 0.5 NM limit with the altitude 300 feet high. Airspeed remained 20 knots above the LAP pattern value until the IP called for the power reduction, and the exit heading from the turn to final was 10 degrees off. The deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and the recognition was delayed.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not give the standardized position reports at the points described in the LAP and delayed the checks of the other traffic in the pattern. Altitude reached the 300 feet deviation limit on the downwind leg and airspeed the 20 knots limit, and the corrections were made only after the IP's verbal indications. Proper spacing was regained late, with the result that the pattern had to be extended on the IP's instruction.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern within the desired standards, giving all the standardized position reports and maintaining proper spacing to the preceding traffic. Altitude twice reached 250 feet and airspeed 18 knots of deviation on the crosswind and base legs, close to the limits for the code, although each deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the pattern altitude and airspeed is expected to improve with the following repetitions.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern accurately and promptly, overflying every point described in the LAP within 0.2 NM and complying with all the ATC instructions without prompting. Altitude was held within 110 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading from each turn within 4 degrees. Proper spacing to the other traffic was maintained while clearing constantly and all the standardized position reports were given at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern with exceptional precision, with negligible deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading and with every LAP point overflown within 0.1 NM. The radio was monitored continuously and the position of each A/C in the pattern was checked against its position report and the ATC instructions, so that spacing was managed in advance and required no correction. All the transmissions were made in standardized phraseology at the correct points. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect crosswind correction technique on the downwind leg, did not overfly the points of the traffic pattern as they are described in the LAP, drifting 1.5 NM outside the published track. Altitude was 450 feet low and airspeed 30 knots below the LAP pattern value at the base turn, with the result that the IP directed the repositioning and executed the turn to final. Spacing to the preceding traffic was not re-established by the SP without assistance.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not maintain proper spacing to the other traffic in the pattern and did not clear constantly. The aircraft closed inside the briefed spacing on the preceding A/C while the altitude was 380 feet high, with the result that the IP took control and directed the break-out. The required position report was made by the IP because the SP did not respond to the ATC instruction.

SP, due to a delayed power reduction abeam the landing threshold, did not maintain the LAP pattern airspeed and altitude on the downwind leg, reaching deviations of 20 knots and 300 feet. The base turn was started at the 0.5 NM limit from the point described in the LAP and the exit heading from the turn to final was 10 degrees off. The deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and the recognition was delayed.

SP, due to non-standard phraseology that left the intention ambiguous to the controller, did not give the standardized position reports required in the pattern and read back the sequencing instruction incorrectly. The error was identified and corrected only after the IP's verbal indication, by which time the aircraft was 300 feet above the LAP pattern altitude and 0.5 NM outside the downwind track. Proper spacing to the traffic ahead was restored with delay.

SP, due to a shallow bank in the turn to base, did not overfly the base turn point as it is described in the LAP, rolling out 0.35 NM outside the published track. Altitude deviated by 200 feet and airspeed by 15 knots during the correction. The errors were minor and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to a failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not hold the LAP pattern altitude and airspeed on the downwind leg, allowing deviations of 220 feet and 16 knots. Two standardized position reports were given late relative to the points described in the LAP. The deviations were recognized by the SP and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern accurately and promptly, overflying the LAP points within 0.4 NM and giving all the standardized position reports. Altitude deviations reached 140 feet and airspeed 9 knots, close to the limits for the code, and the exit heading from the turn to final twice required a 5 degree correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a closer LAP track and tighter airspeed control are expected in the following sorties.

SP flew the airport traffic pattern with exceptional precision, overflying every point described in the LAP within 0.1 NM with negligible deviations in altitude, airspeed and exit heading. The radio was monitored continuously and the position of every A/C in the pattern was checked against its position report and the ATC instructions, so that proper spacing was maintained without any correction being required. All the standardized position reports were given in full at the correct points while clearing constantly. Above end of block MIF achieved.
